/**
 * Model catalog for the PostHog gateway provider.
 *
 * Model ids come straight from the `posthog_code` allowlist
 * (`services/llm-gateway/src/llm_gateway/products/config.py`). Metadata
 * (context window, max tokens, cost, reasoning, thinkingLevelMap, compat)
 * mirrors pi's own built-in definitions for these exact ids so behaviour
 * matches what pi does when talking to the providers directly. Costs are
 * USD per million tokens and are used only for pi's local display — real
 * billing/metering happens gateway-side.
 *
 * - Claude → Anthropic Messages API (`anthropic-messages`), best fidelity for
 *   extended thinking + tool use.
 * - GPT-5.x → OpenAI Chat Completions API (`openai-completions`) via the
 *   gateway's `/{product}/v1/chat/completions` endpoint.
 */
import type { ProviderModelConfig } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";

/** GPT-5.x over chat/completions: gpt-5 rejects `max_tokens` (needs
 * `max_completion_tokens`), supports `reasoning_effort` and the developer role.
 * We set these explicitly because pi only auto-detects compat for
 * `api.openai.com`, not for the gateway host. */
const GPT_COMPAT = {
    maxTokensField: "max_completion_tokens",
    supportsReasoningEffort: true,
    supportsDeveloperRole: true,
    supportsUsageInStreaming: true,
} as const;

type ClaudeSpec = Omit<ProviderModelConfig, "api" | "baseUrl">;
type GptSpec = Omit<ProviderModelConfig, "api" | "baseUrl">;

/**
 * Build the full model list bound to a region's gateway endpoints. Claude
 * models use the Anthropic base; GPT models override to `openai-completions`
 * on the OpenAI base. `oauth.modifyModels` rebuilds `baseUrl` per credential,
 * so this same shape is produced for whichever region the user logs into.
 */
export function buildModels(anthropicBase: string, openaiBase: string): ProviderModelConfig[] {
    const claude = CLAUDE_MODELS.map((m) => ({ ...m, api: "anthropic-messages" as const, baseUrl: anthropicBase }));
    const gpt = GPT_MODELS.map((m) => ({ ...m, api: "openai-completions" as const, baseUrl: openaiBase }));
    return [...claude, ...gpt];
}

/** Anthropic-api model ids (used by `modifyModels` to pick the right base). */
export const CLAUDE_MODEL_IDS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(CLAUDE_MODELS.map((m) => m.id));

# pi-posthog-llm-gateway

Use **PostHog's LLM gateway** as a provider in the [pi coding agent](https://pi.dev).

Log in with your PostHog account and code against Claude and GPT models served
through PostHog's gateway — **billed through PostHog**, with usage and cost
tracked automatically in PostHog's LLM analytics. No Anthropic/OpenAI API keys
to manage; authentication is PostHog OAuth.

Under the hood this registers a `posthog` provider that talks to
`gateway.<region>.posthog.com` under the **`posthog_code`** product (the same
product PostHog's own coding agents use), authenticated with a `pha_` OAuth
access token. The scope requested at login is chosen per region: `us`/`eu`
request `llm_gateway:read` (the scope the gateway checks for, which the prod
apps carry on their ceiling), while `dev` requests `*` (the local app is seeded
with an empty scope ceiling, where `llm_gateway:read` is rejected but `*` is
grandfathered in). Override for any region with `POSTHOG_OAUTH_SCOPE`.

## Install

```sh
# from git
pi install git:github.com/PostHog/pi-posthog-llm-gateway

# or from a local checkout
pi install /path/to/pi-posthog-llm-gateway
```

You can also drop it into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` (as a folder with this
package) for a global install, or load it ad-hoc without installing:

```sh
pi -e /path/to/pi-posthog-llm-gateway/src/index.ts
```

## Log in and use

```
/login posthog      # opens your browser; pick your region if not preset
/model              # choose a PostHog model (e.g. "Claude Opus 4.8 (PostHog)")
```

Then just chat. `/posthog-gateway` prints the resolved region, endpoints, and
available model ids. Log out with `/logout posthog`.

The login uses authorization-code + PKCE with a loopback callback on
`http://localhost:8237` (falling back to `8239`). On a headless/remote box where
the browser can't reach localhost, paste the redirect URL or code when prompted.

## Models

Served through the gateway's `posthog_code` allowlist:

- **Claude** (Anthropic Messages API): Opus 4.5 / 4.6 / 4.7 / 4.8, Fable 5,
  Sonnet 4.5 / 4.6 / 5, Haiku 4.5.
- **GPT** (OpenAI Chat Completions API): GPT-5.2, GPT-5.3 Codex, GPT-5.4,
  GPT-5.5, GPT-5 Mini.

## Configuration (environment variables)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POSTHOG_GATEWAY_REGION` | *(prompt at login)* | `us`, `eu`, or `dev`. If set, skips the region prompt. |
| `POSTHOG_OAUTH_BASE_URL` | per region | Override the OAuth server (advanced / self-hosted). |
| `POSTHOG_GATEWAY_BASE_URL` | per region | Override the gateway host (advanced / self-hosted). |
| `POSTHOG_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` | `array`/`posthog_code` public client | Override the OAuth client id (see below). |
| `POSTHOG_OAUTH_SCOPE` | `llm_gateway:read` (us/eu), `*` (dev) | Scope requested at login. Override e.g. for a dedicated app with a different ceiling. |

Region maps to: US → `us.posthog.com` + `gateway.us.posthog.com`, EU →
`eu.posthog.com` + `gateway.eu.posthog.com`, dev → `localhost:8010` +
`localhost:3308`. Your region is stored on the credential at login, so refresh
and model routing use the right hosts automatically.

## Billing

Every generation flows through PostHog's gateway and is metered as an
`$ai_generation` event with `ai_product = posthog_code`, attributed to your
PostHog team. View spend in PostHog under **LLM analytics** / **AI gateway**.
Cost numbers shown inside pi are for local display only; PostHog is the source
of truth. Product- and user-level cost rate limits apply gateway-side.

## Notes

- **OAuth client id.** By default this reuses PostHog's public `array` /
  `posthog_code` OAuth client (a public client — the id is not a secret, exactly
  as a native app embeds one). To attribute pi traffic to a dedicated app,
  register a public OAuth application (with the `llm_gateway:read` scope on
  its ceiling and a `http://localhost:8237/callback` redirect URI), add its
  application id to a product allowlist in the gateway's `products/config.py`,
  and set `POSTHOG_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` — no code change required. (The default
  `llm_gateway:read` scope already fits such an app on us/eu; set
  `POSTHOG_OAUTH_SCOPE` only if your app's ceiling needs a different scope.)
- **No runtime dependencies.** The OAuth flow uses only Node built-ins
  (`node:http`, `node:crypto`); pi packages are peer/dev dependencies for types.
